name: Albany
reason: Rule 1 and towns: Wikivoyage has a full Albany article and Tourism WA's Great Southern page names it; the region's main base, WA's oldest European settlement, with the National Anzac Centre, whaling station and Torndirrup nearby.

name: Bluff Knoll
reason: Rules 1-2: DBCA site page, Tourism WA and Australia's South West all feature it; the highest peak in southern WA with a 6 km return summit walk.

name: Desert Mounted Corps War Memorial
reason: Rules 1-3: Wikivoyage Albany names it with 'good views from this point' and Visit Albany's Mount Clarence Heritage & Granite Trail is built around it; the Port Said monument, shipped to Albany in 1959 and standing on Mount Clarence, is a landmark, not a minor plaque. Objection: it could be folded into a Mount Clarence / Albany Heritage Park spot.

name: Little Beach
reason: Rules 1-2: DBCA site and park pages, Australia's South West and Visit Albany ('regularly ranked as one of Western Australia's best beaches'); a headline beach.

name: Old Post Office, Albany
reason: For: Wikivoyage names the 1869 building with its spiral tower stair. Against: one counted source, and it now houses restaurants (the museum's current status is unconfirmed), so a visitor may only see a heritage facade or a dining room (rule 2: a heritage building qualifies only if the public can go in or it is a named stop of a guide's walking route).
